themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you measure often changes while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: On the loss of B2B account and buying-group intent signal all three models say outcomes are sparse, delayed and biased toward accounts already pursued, echoing answer engine optimization (no impressions or stable denominator), cross-channel incrementality (platforms react to the test), and identity resolution (no natural signal that a match was wrong).

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared schema or central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models say assistants gain by posing as humans and no one can issue trusted credentials; on cross-channel journey orchestration channel owners are paid to say yes; on the semantic context layer all three call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement, not a modeling gap.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe, auditable agent execution all three models open with a proxy or gateway holding credentials, logs, budget caps and a kill switch; the same instinct shows up as a single egress gate in downstream consent enforcement and one shared pre-send eligibility check in journey orchestration.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: On provable downstream consent and deletion the models say you cannot inspect an ad platform audience or an agency segment and cannot locate a person inside a trained model; the same opacity blocks cross-channel incrementality, where platforms control the treatment and hide how it changes.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On governance of generative marketing content all three models propose a locked library of approved claims and then admit that deciding whether wording crosses a legal line is a reasoning task software cannot defend in an audit; the semantic context layer answers make the parallel point that one global definition cannot hold.
